title: Shutdown mass-layoff policy rescinded as part of settlement with unions
summary: The Trump administration sent reduction in force notices to thousands of employees during the 43-day government shutdown last fall.

title: Following court order, OPM replaces 'favorite EO' question for jobseekers
summary: The Office of Personnel Management’s latest essay question for federal job applicants asks less about their personal politics and more about their ability to follow instructions.

title: Watchdog won’t discipline agencies over partisan shutdown posts but warns against ‘derogatory’ messaging
summary: Many departments blamed congressional Democrats for last year’s funding lapse by posting banners on agency websites and modifying furloughed employees’ out-of-office messages.

title: FDA nominee faces bipartisan scrutiny over vaccines and abortion drug
summary: Heidi Overton drew pointed questions from senators on vaccine safety and mifepristone during her confirmation hearing Thursday.

title: ICE’s $45 billion detention expansion is littered with costly missteps, watchdog reports
summary: The Government Accountability Office criticized plans to sell recently purchased warehouses, the shuttered “Alligator Alcatraz” facility and spending millions to detain an average of 16 migrants in fiscal 2026 at Guantanamo Bay.

title: VA’s contracting crackdown gave some staff hours to do hundreds of reviews
summary: VA's watchdog office noted these reviews happened quickly under strict deadlines, but generally complied with requirements for terminating contracts.

title: GSA claims it found $1.2B in suspected COVID-related contracting fraud
summary: The agency previously said it found $13 billion in suspected procurement-related fraud and is investigating other sources of potential fraud.

title: Your federal benefits changed this year. Here’s what to know
summary: A guide to the retirement, insurance, Social Security and TSP changes affecting federal employees, retirees and survivors in 2026, plus what to watch for in 2027.

title: FLRA ruling puts ball back in courts’ court on Trump’s union EOs
summary: The National Treasury Employees Union said Wednesday that a recent Federal Labor Relations Authority decision supports its argument that it cannot seek redress through administrative channels.

title: Trust in government is sinking, but a new survey suggests civil servants’ stock is rising
summary: The percentages of respondents who said most civil servants are competent and committed to helping people “like me” increased to record highs — at 65% and 61%, respectively.

title: IRS and Social Security will see more employees quit without advanced leave, senators warn
summary: Senate Democrats warn employees will “inevitably leave” both agencies following a suspension of advanced leave, adding to deep staffing cuts.

title: ShinyHunters claims FBI data theft, demands bureau retract cyber warning
summary: The hacking group says it obtained sensitive employee and applicant records. The full scope of the claimed breach remains unclear.

title: FAA administrator defends withholding part of ATC pay raise
summary: Democrats on a House appropriations subcommittee accused FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford of trying to “squeeze” the already overstretched air traffic controller workforce.

title: Login.gov is now accepting mobile driver’s licenses
summary: The feature builds on the federal government’s effort to mandate that agencies use the digital identity verification platform.

title: Congress — not the president — should appoint the next GAO head, bipartisan coalition argues
summary: The organizations from across the political spectrum contended that former Comptroller General Gene Dodaro’s retirement last year provides an opportunity for lawmakers to overhaul the nomination process.

title: Trump wants an ‘AI Force.’ What would that actually look like?
summary: The president compared the proposed unit to Space Force, but offered few details about its mission, authority or place in the federal government.

title: IRS watchdog audits employee reassignments, as agency looks to extend some tours of duty
summary: Employees placed on these involuntary details are doing jobs several pay grades below the work they were hired to perform, but continue to receive their regular paychecks.

title: Lawmakers call on leadership to override Trump’s planned pay freeze
summary: Members of both parties urged congressional leaders to “at minimum” authorize an across-the-board 3.8% pay raise for civilian federal employees, in line with President Trump’s supplemental pay increase planned only for law enforcement.

title: OPM uses conservative influencers on college tour to recruit young workers
summary: On Thursday, the government HR agency chief is visiting an unaccredited college founded by right-wing figures.

title: A second lawsuit challenges plans to put ICE agents near polling places
summary: The filing comes after administration officials said federal agents could conduct immigration enforcement at polling locations in certain circumstances.

title: NASA employees: EEOC committed ‘flagrant distortions’ to decertify class complaint
summary: EEOC officials touted a long-running discrimination case against NASA as an example why federal sector cases were in need of reform. The employees who brought the case said commissioners railroaded them.
